report.sources_described: Three water sources used interchangeably or blended: protected groundwater wells within Santa Clara (20 active wells, 500-900 feet deep, supplying most of the water), Sierra Nevada snowmelt via the SFPUC Hetch Hetchy System (typically serving the area north of Highway 101; fluoridated), and Valley Water treated surface water from the Rinconada Water Treatment Plant (Calero Reservoir and Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta imports; serving primarily the south-west portion of the City). Together they provide an average of 15 million gallons per day.
violations: Tier 3 Notice from SFPUC (PDF page 5): The SFPUC notified the City of a monitoring violation, as is required within one year of discovery. Because of equipment failure, the San Francisco Regional Water System (SFRWS) operated by the SFPUC did not monitor for recycled filter backwash water turbidity at its Sunol Valley Water Treatment Plant (SVWTP) from June 23 to July 2, 2025. It was corrected July 3, 2025, once it became apparent to plant staff. There was no emergency or impact to SFPUC's water quality; downstream monitoring indicated SVWTP effluent was consistently of very high quality and exceeded all drinking water standards.

Lead (PDF page 5): 'No Santa Clara water sources have exceeded the ACTION LEVEL for lead.' Residential-tap sampling (52 taps, 2022): lead 90th percentile ND, 0 exceedances; copper 90th percentile 0.34 ppm, 0 exceedances.

School lead testing 2018 (PDF page 4 table, note 6): 33 schools, 172 samples; 90th percentile ND; Number Exceeded = 1 - the 2018 sampling result for John Sutter Elementary was 26 ppb; repeat sampling following plumbing repairs was non-detect for lead.

Report states all water meets applicable drinking water standards; only constituents detected in at least one water source appear in the table. Hexavalent chromium: all 20 groundwater wells tested below the 10 ppb MCL (PDF page 6).

report.extraction_notes: Single-source (groundwater) system; tables have one results column, so source_group is null throughout. The report's results column is headed 'Amount Detected' (or 'Detected') with a separate 'Range Low-High' column; Amount Detected is treated as the average (value_basis 'average', average filled) except where the row itself names another basis (90th percentile for lead/copper, annual running average for free chlorine, highest monthly percent positive for total coliform). Leading-dot numbers (.15, .11, .0027, .38, .015, .23, .0046) are stored as decimals; ND range-lows are stored as 0. PFHxS average is printed ',0073' (comma) and stored as 0.0073. The 'Other Substances' table (alkalinity, bicarbonate, calcium, hardness, magnesium, potassium, sodium) has no MCL/PHG columns. Lead and copper were sampled in 2023 (year printed in the table); all other rows 2025. No E. coli, radon, VOC, or secondary manganese/zinc rows are printed (report lists detected contaminants only).
